- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate during mean-reversion phases; adjust downward when recent history shows consolidation or decline.
- Overshoot after volatility spikes; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below the immediate prior high.
- Lagged response to true price movements: model reacts too slowly to downward trends; apply a 1–2 day lead correction for downward momentum.
- High forecast variance in early horizon (e.g., 1–5 days) correlates with true volatility; dampen forecast variance by smoothing with 3-day moving average.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 5 days are above 70, cap forecast at 70.5 unless confirmed breakout.
